_readme: The 'Why? (CBSE rule)' column for the À retenir correction tables. Keyed by the exact « wrong » form found in letterdata.js notes. DRAFTED BY CLAUDE — reviewed by the teacher before use. Edit any value here and re-run the build; no code changes needed. A pair with no entry renders with an empty Why cell rather than a guess.
système d'éducatif: An adjective follows its noun directly — never insert de between them.
commencer son scolaire: Scolaire is an adjective. The noun is la scolarité, so the possessive is sa.
J'attends pour ta réponse: Attendre is transitive in French — no preposition. English “wait for” is the trap.
Comment ça-va ?: No hyphen here. The hyphen belongs only to inversion, as in va-t-il.
commencer sont scolaires: Sont is the verb être; the possessive is son/sa. The noun is la scolarité.
J'attends pour ta lettre: Attendre takes a direct object — j'attends ta lettre, with no pour.
les annonces classées: A calque of English “classified ads”. The French idiom is les petites annonces.
il faut que tu le commences: After il faut que the verb takes the subjonctif: faire → fasses.
Bonne Chance: French capitalises only the first word of a phrase — chance stays lowercase.
cela me plait: Plaire keeps its circumflex in the third person: il plaît.
C'est une plus ancienne université: A superlative needs the definite article: la plus ancienne, not une plus.
crée: Past participle of créer agreeing with a feminine subject: créée — é then ée.
Je fais de l'achat: Fixed expression, always plural: faire des achats.
une poste: Gender changes the meaning: un poste = a job, la poste = the post office.
d'y joindre: Postuler is the verb for applying for a job; joindre means to attach or to reach.
des notes que dois rédiger: French never drops the subject pronoun — que tu dois rédiger.
Discute de ce travail à tes parents: You discuter avec someone de something — never discuter à.
Bisou !: A written sign-off takes a comma, and the standard form is Bises,.
Yoga: Common nouns are not capitalised in French: le yoga.
passe: The past participle carries the accent: passé. Without it, it is the present tense.
a votre / a 4 heures / a tes parents: à with a grave accent is the preposition; a without one is the verb avoir.
rien m'a remis: Negation needs ne, and the participle agrees with the preceding feminine object: rien ne m'a remise.
Toute la nuit s'est passé: A pronominal verb takes être, so the participle agrees with the subject la nuit → passée.
alors, il faut: No comma after alors when it opens the clause.
deux maisons: The parliamentary word is chambre — maison is a calque of English “House”.
le Lok Sabha: Chambre is feminine, so the assembly takes la.
